Operator:  
Good morning, and welcome to the EssenCorp Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for those wishing to ask a question will be given later. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Vice President of Investor Relations.

Sarah Johnson:  
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss EssenCorp's Q3 results. With me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Patel, Chief Marketing Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. EssenCorp delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover five key aspects: supply chain efficiencies and productivity savings impact; capital expenditure plans and priorities; key strategic priorities and progress; new product launches and innovation pipeline update; and price elasticity observations.

Thank you again for your time. I will now turn the call over to Maria Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Maria Chen:  
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $7.8 billion, representing a 6% increase compared to the prior year. Gross margin was 52.0%, driven by supply chain efficiencies, pricing actions, and favorable mix. Operating income was $1.4 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $1.62. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Turning to some of the key highlights, let me start with one of our major value drivers: supply chain efficiencies and productivity savings. This quarter, these initiatives provided a $178 million tailwind to our adjusted operating income—up 22% year-over-year—and added about 45 basis points to our adjusted EPS. This builds on the $650 million in run-rate savings we've secured year-to-date, positioning us ahead of our full-year target of $800 million to $900 million.

Our supply chain accounts for roughly 28% of COGS across our portfolio, including household essentials like FreshGlow laundry detergents and PureGlow personal care products, snacks under NutriBar, and beverages in our Quench lineup. With palm oil prices up 15% year-over-year from El Niño effects in Southeast Asia and ocean freight rates still 10-12% higher than pre-pandemic levels according to the Drewry World Container Index, these efficiencies have been essential in supporting our 520 basis point gross margin expansion this quarter.

On procurement optimization, our Global Strategic Sourcing team consolidated volumes with major suppliers, delivering an 8% blended cost reduction on key inputs like surfactants and corn derivatives. For example, multi-year contracts renewed with palm oil leaders such as Wilmar International and Cargill incorporated ESG-linked pricing, trimming 2-3% off spot rates and advancing our Scope 3 emissions reduction by 18% in tropical commodities. That generated $65 million in savings.

In manufacturing, we achieved a 14% improvement in Overall Equipment Effectiveness across our 120 plants worldwide through lean six sigma initiatives and targeted automation. In North America, robotic depalletizers at our Ohio and Texas sites—inspired by Procter & Gamble's Ariel lines—increased throughput by 20% on high-volume items like FreshGlow pods. In Europe, advanced process control software at our Dijon facility cut energy intensity by 12% per ton, critical given rising EU carbon border adjustment costs.

Logistics and distribution contributed $52 million in savings. AI-powered routing from tools like FourKites and Manhattan Associates reduced truckload miles by 11% in the U.S. and dwell times by 9% at distribution centers. In Asia-Pacific, where e-commerce now makes up over 25% of CPG sales per Nielsen, our partnership with JD Logistics in China has expanded micro-fulfillment centers, lifting on-time-in-full delivery to 98.5% from 94% last year and saving 15% on inbound freight from Indonesia.

Inventory management completed the picture, with our AI-driven demand sensing in SAP IBP boosting forecast accuracy to 92% at the SKU-store level and increasing inventory turns from 8.7x to 10.2x globally. This released $320 million in working capital, especially helpful in emerging markets facing disruptions like India's monsoons.

Regionally, North America led with 45% of savings at $80 million, driven by nearshoring resin pouch production from Mexico to ease U.S. port issues. Europe added 30% or $53 million via circular packaging—our rPET recycling with Veolia cut virgin plastic costs by 7% and met UK Plastic Packaging Tax rules. APAC contributed 18% or $32 million through scale in Vietnam and India plants offsetting 20%+ caustic soda inflation. Latin America was 7%, tempered by Argentina's currency swings, but we're countering with local sourcing for Quench beverages.

Compared to peers, we're outperforming—McKinsey reports industry-average productivity savings at 5-7% year-over-year, but our $450 million in digital twins and IoT over the past 24 months has us at 12-15%, similar to Unilever's post-2022 approach but enhanced by private-label synergies amid Aldi and Lidl gains.

Strategically, 60% of savings are reinvested: 30% into innovation like bio-based enzymes for next-gen FreshGlow, 20% into velocity marketing to maintain 68% household penetration per IRI, and 10% into share repurchases. The balance strengthens the P&L against risks like U.S. tariffs on Chinese imports.

For Q4 and FY25, we anticipate over $200 million in additional run-rate savings, with potential from gen-AI in supplier collaboration, like predictive pricing akin to Colgate's palm oil tools. Red Sea reroutings add 5-7 days to EU paths, but multi-modal hedging protects us. These aren't mere cost cuts; they're a moat in a 2.5% volume growth CPG world per Kantar, reflected in our 18% operating margin.

Shifting to price elasticity observations, which have underpinned our pricing strategy in this macro reset. With global inflation at 2.5% but grocery at 4-5%, we've used machine learning on 15+ years of IRI and Nielsen data for granular SKU-channel insights.

Across our $28 billion portfolio—personal care at 35%, home care 30%, food and snacks 35%—elasticity averaged -1.1 this quarter, better than -1.4 last year and -1.3 in Q2. A 1% ASP rise meant just 1.1% volume drop, fueling 9% pricing to organic growth versus -2% volume/mix. That's stronger than the -1.3 industry average per Kantar, helping us gain share in 7 of 10 top categories.

Premiumization post-pandemic is key: consumers favor value-premium like PureGlow hyaluronic serums, up 12% ASP with flat volume. We took 7-10% list hikes on 65% of SKUs, netting 8% after trade optimization.

By category: Personal care at -0.9 elasticity—HerbalEssence-like revitalizing line up 9% ASP with 1% volume dip, HHP to 42%. Mass rivals like Suave hit -1.6. AI dynamic pricing in 200 Walmart/Kroger markets uses 50 million loyalty swipes. Home care -1.2, TideGuard pods flat volume on 10% hike, but liquids -3% prompting trade spend to 18%. Enzyme variants at +15% ASP grew tonnage 1%. Snacks -1.4, CrunchBar -4% on 7%, but premium NovaNuts-like -0.7 with +6%.

Regions: North America -1.0 (55% sales), U.S. accepted 9% hikes with -2% shrinkage via EDLP at Costco/Walmart; Canada -1.3. EMEA -1.2, UK -1.0, Germany -1.5 countered by app promotions. APAC -1.3, India -0.9 via kiranas. LatAm -1.4, bundles key.

Our $50 million Elasticity Prediction Engine uses satellite shelf monitoring, social sentiment, scanner data for 85% forecast accuracy. Blockchain pilots measure net pricing.

Our Smart Pricing 2.0 targets -1.0 for premium, -1.3 for value. Better than P&G's -1.2 average. Q4: -1.05 on 5-7% pricing for 4-6% growth.

Next, our new product launches and innovation pipeline. In CPG, innovation drives growth against disruptors, meeting demands for health, sustainability, convenience. New products (last 24 months) were 18% of Q3 sales, up from 14%, adding 150bps to gross margins via premiums and efficient chains.

Q3 stars: VitalGlow Hydration+ skincare for Gen Z skinimalism—national NA rollout July, 85% ACV in drug/mass in 8 weeks per IRI, 25% ahead benchmark, 32% repeats like Olay, $12-18 price, $45M incremental, $180M FY run-rate. Strong in U.S. Sunbelt.

PureHarvest Plant-Powered Protein Shakes—pea/hemp zero-sugar for $20B plant-protein market. EMEA/APAC Q2 launch, 65% ACV UK/Germany, 40% velocity vs Alpro, 12 units/store/week, $28M Q3 (60% beat), 45% e-comm China via AR/KOLs.

EcoShield Multi-Surface Wipes—compostable 98% bio-based for EU plastics directive/U.S. moms. LATAM/NA, 72% club distro Costco/Sam's, 22% HHP lift, $22M Q3, +300bps margins via bamboo.

Disciplined NPI with consumer co-creation, $450M R&D YTD (3.2% sales, Unilever level), $2.8B NPV pipeline, 45 SKUs.

Pipeline: Health & Wellness 50%—NeuroNourish Nootropics H1'25 NA/Australia, lion's mane/adaptogens, 15% cognitive lift study, $15B space, $250M Y1 at $3.99, 30% velocity. Sustainability 30%—CycleSafe Laundry Pods refillable PCR, 40% cold efficacy, France pilots 28% repeats, $100M fund, $150M India. Digital 20%—SmartKitchen Snacks app-synced AR flavors, Google Cloud, 35% faster formulation, 55% DTC/Instacart.

70% pipeline +20-30% premiums, regional like halal MENA, nearshored 60%. New products to 20-22% 2025 sales, 8-10% organic vs 4-5% industry.

Forward-looking subject to risks—see 10-Q.

On capital expenditure plans and priorities for FY24 and beyond. In CPG, disciplined capex sustains mid-single-digit organic growth amid PET/pulp inflation 8-10% and bottlenecks.

FY24 capex $1.25B, 4.2% of ~$30B sales, +9% from FY23 $1.15B. Weighted to growth/productivity, 38% or $475M maintenance, flat % sales, 85% asset utilization.

Four priorities align with 'Win the Everyday'—premiumization, sustainability, digital—like P&G/Unilever.

Capacity expansion 32% $400M: Monterrey Mexico $150M greenfield, 4 aseptic lines PureSpring plant-based, +20% NA capex e-comm 25% CAGR. Jakarta $80M K-beauty skincare, $50B APAC premium 7%.

Automation/resilience 25% $310M: 150 AMRs Locus U.S. DCs +30% throughput PepsiCo-style; Rotterdam cold-hub $70M perishables, -5-7 WC days vs 15% freight rise.

ESG 18% $225M: Solar/wastewater 20 NA plants $90M, -25% Scope 1 by '26 Nestlé-like; bio-PET FreshGlow $60M -40% virgin, U.S. mandates.

Digital/innovation 9% $115M: SAP S/4HANA AI $50M, 82-92% forecast IRI/Circana; Cincinnati R&D $30M precision fermentation snacks.

Regions: NA 52% $650M 6% growth; Europe 28% $350M premium share; EM 20% $250M Brazil/India JVs.

$1.25B targets 12-15% ROIC >10% WACC, $200M productivity FY24, EBITDA accretion 18-24 months.

I will now turn the call over to David Patel to discuss marketing and brand performance.

David Patel:  
Thank you, Maria. We saw strong performance in our FreshGlow and PureGlow brands this quarter. Our recent GlowUp campaign has resonated well with consumers, driving trial and loyalty through targeted digital and in-store activations. We are also excited about the launch of our VitalGlow Hydration+ line, which is already generating positive feedback and contributing meaningfully to category growth with its clean formulations and premium positioning.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:  
Thank you. Instructions for those asking questions: Press star then 1 on your touchtone phone. Our first question comes from Jane Doe with Goldman Sachs.

Jane Doe:  
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the details of the new marketing campaign and its impact on sales?

David Patel:  
Good morning, Jane. The GlowUp campaign for PureGlow focuses on authentic storytelling around skinimalism and clean beauty, leveraging TikTok influencers, AR try-ons, and in-store sampling at key retailers like Walmart and Ulta. We've seen a 25% lift in awareness per our post-campaign surveys, translating to 15% sales uplift in the skincare portfolio quarter-over-quarter. It's particularly strong online, where e-comm sales for PureGlow jumped 35%, helping us gain 1.2 share points in the segment.

Operator:  
Our next question comes from John Smith with JPMorgan.

John Smith:  
What are your plans for addressing rising commodity costs in the coming quarters?

Maria Chen:  
Thanks, John. As I detailed earlier, our supply chain initiatives are front and center—procurement optimizations and manufacturing productivity have already offset much of the 15% palm oil rise and elevated freight. For Q4 and beyond, we'll continue leveraging multi-year ESG contracts, nearshoring, and AI logistics to deliver another $200 million-plus in savings. We're also monitoring Red Sea risks but hedged across modes, ensuring we protect margins without passing on unnecessary costs.

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen:  
How is the current inflationary environment impacting consumer demand for your premium product lines?

Alex Rivera:  
Hi Emily. Inflation has tested resilience, but our premium lines like VitaFuel and PureGlow are holding strong with elasticity around -0.9 to -1.0, as Maria noted. Consumers are trading up for value in health and clean beauty, with 42% household penetration gains. Our pricing discipline—7-10% hikes with minimal volume loss—plus innovation like VitalGlow supports 6.2% organic growth. We're gaining share as private labels pressure value tiers.

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Mike Lee with Barclays.

Mike Lee:  
Can you discuss the performance of your e-commerce channel this quarter?

David Patel:  
Sure, Mike. E-commerce hit 25% of sales, up 500bps year-over-year, outpacing the 18% U.S. CPG average. Shopper 360 platform drove 22% higher conversions via personalization from 15 million loyalty users. Amazon velocity for NutriBar up 32%, top-10 ranking. DTC via TikTok Shop and Instacart added $45 million incremental, with same-day for 70% SKUs boosting repeats 14%. Gen-AI demand forecasting at 92% accuracy cut stockouts 30%.

Operator:  
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your questions and participation in today's call. Before we wrap, let me provide some color on our key strategic priorities and the progress we've made year-to-date. At EssenCorp, we're focused on sustainable, profitable growth amid inflation, value-seeking, and supply chain volatility.

Our five pillars: portfolio premiumization and innovation; sustainability leadership; digital acceleration; supply chain resilience; geographic expansion. This supports raised FY guidance: 5-7% organic sales, 8-10% core EPS.

Premiumization: Power brands 42% sales, up from 35%, 60% growth. VitaFuel new SKUs 15% ACV in 90 days, 28% revenue +12% AUR, HHP +4 to 22% via Kroger/Walmart. PureGlow 35% growth, Gen Z clean beauty. Divested canned soups $450M, targeting 22% margins FY25.

Sustainability: 100% recyclable NA packaging ahead schedule, -25% virgin plastic YTD, $28M savings, NPS +15 to 72. BASF bio-PET AquaPure -40% carbon, +1200 EMEA points, 1.5 share vs Nestlé. APAC GreenLeaf 50% recycled, 18% China share.

Digital: 25% sales e-comm, Shopper 360 22% conversions. Amazon snacks +32%, Snapchat AR $45M DTC. Google AI 92% ZIP forecasts, +2 gross margin.

Supply chain: $220M gross savings YTD >$200M target, 65% contracts 8-10% cuts. RSPO palm 40%, Mexico robotics +18% throughput. LatAm +12% despite FX.

Geographic: NA +4% 62% sales; Europe +7% 1.2 UK share; APAC +11% China double; India/SE Asia $150M Hyderabad plant 20% modern trade.

Synergies position us for 12-15% ROIC. Q3: 6.2% organic, +1.4 share, margins +110bps to 19.8%.

We're confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Sarah Johnson:  
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the EssenCorp Q3 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
